title: E-commerce
description:
# E-commerce Customer Support & Marketplace Assistant – Dutch Market



We are a growing Dutch e-commerce company selling consumer products across multiple online marketplaces. We are looking for a reliable, proactive, and versatile **E-commerce Assistant** who can become an important part of our day-to-day operations.



We are not looking for someone who can only follow a fixed set of tasks. We are looking for someone who understands e-commerce, takes responsibility, learns quickly, and is comfortable handling different tasks when needed.



## Your main responsibilities



Your most important responsibility will be **customer service and day-to-day marketplace management**.



You will:



- Manage our customer service inbox and respond to customers

- Answer customer questions about our products, orders, deliveries, returns, warranties, and other issues

- Handle customer cases professionally and look for solutions

- Manage customer questions and cases on BOL marketplace and Amazon

- Help manage our **Amazon Seller Central** accounts

- Monitor orders, returns, customer messages, account notifications, and other marketplace issues

- Help maintain product listings and product information

- Identify recurring customer or product issues and communicate these to our team

- Perform general e-commerce and administrative tasks when necessary



## Amazon & BOL Marketplace



Experience with **Amazon Seller Central** is very important to us.



You should already understand the basics of working inside an Amazon seller account and preferably have experience with things such as:



- Managing listings

- Handling customer messages

- Orders and returns

- Account notifications

- Seller performance

- Basic troubleshooting

- Updating product information



Experience with **BOL marketplace** is a big advantage. If you have strong Amazon experience but have never worked with BOL marketplace before, that is okay as long as you are willing and able to learn it quickly.



## Dutch customer service



Our customers are mainly Dutch, so a large part of the customer communication will be in **Dutch**.



You do not necessarily need to be a native Dutch speaker, but you must be comfortable working with Dutch customer messages and using translation/AI tools where necessary to write clear and professional responses.



Being able to understand the customer's problem and provide the correct solution is more important than translating everything manually.



## Social media – future opportunity



In the future, we would also like this role to grow into helping manage our social media channels.



This could include:



- Preparing and publishing posts

- Writing captions

- Scheduling content

- Keeping our social media pages active

- Helping with basic community management



Social media experience is therefore a plus, but **it is not the main focus of the role right now**.



Our priorities are:



1. **Customer service**

2. **Amazon Seller Central**

3. **BOL marketplace management**

4. **General e-commerce support**

5. **Social media**



## Who we are looking for



You are a good fit if you:



- Have previous experience working for an **e-commerce company**

- Have hands-on experience with **Amazon Seller Central**

- Have experience with customer service

description:
Job Title:    Credit Repair Specialist & Admin (US Client, Full-Time, Remote)



Type of Work: Full Time



Salary:  $800–$900 USD/month (depending on experience)



Hours per Week: 40



Schedule:   Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM–6:00 PM US Eastern Time

(9:00 PM–6:00 AM PH time during US Daylight Saving Time, roughly March to November; 10:00 PM–7:00 AM PH time the rest of the year)



---



**About Us**



As a US-based credit repair company, we help clients improve their credit by reviewing their reports from Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion and disputing items that are inaccurate, outdated, or unverifiable. Our clients pay nothing upfront and are billed only after a dispute cycle shows results, so careful, consistent work on every file really matters.



The Role



We're looking for an experienced Credit Repair Specialist who can manage client files through each dispute cycle while supporting day-to-day admin tasks like client communication, scheduling, records, and billing support.



What You'll Do



*Credit Repair*

- Review client credit reports from all three bureaus and identify inaccurate, outdated, or unverifiable items

- Prepare dispute letters (including AI-assisted drafts) and check each one for accuracy before sending

- Send disputes to bureaus and creditors via First-Class or Certified Mail, and log tracking numbers and proof of delivery

- Track the 30–45-day investigation window for each cycle and follow up on missing responses

- Re-check client reports each cycle, record changes, and flag favorable results for billing

- Share simple credit-building tips with clients



*Admin & Client Support*

- Respond to inquiries via Meta Inbox,
 comments, SMS, and
 using approved templates

- Manage the Calendly schedule, confirm appointments, and follow up with prospects

- Onboard new clients: collect agreements, ID, proof of address, and credit report access

- Keep client files, notes, and dispute records organized in our CRM / credit repair software

- Support billing by confirming billable cycles and answering basic billing questions

- Send clients progress updates and escalate complaints or complex cases to management

- Handle general tasks such as outgoing mail, document requests, and data entry



**Requirements**

- Proven hands-on experience with US credit repair, including handling disputes with bureaus and creditors from start to finish

- Experience reviewing credit reports, writing dispute letters, tracking responses, and managing client files

- Solid understanding of US credit reports, credit scores, and the dispute process

- Excellent written and spoken English

- Strong attention to detail and ability to manage many files at once

- Reliable computer, stable internet, backup power/internet, and a quiet workspace

- Willingness to work US Eastern hours (night shift in PH)

- Ability to handle sensitive personal and financial information confidentially



**Nice to Have**

- Working knowledge of the FCRA and CROA

- Experience with Credit Repair Cloud, DisputeFox, or similar software

- Experience with Meta Business Suite

- Credit repair certification or related training



**What We Offer**

- $800–$900 USD/month

- Fully remote, long-term position

- Stable Monday–Friday schedule



---

 your resume to 
 with the subject line:

, please answer these questions:

Primary KPI:

Qualified appointments booked



Quality is more important than simply booking appointments. Appointments should ideally be with a business owner or decision-maker who has a legitimate need for business wireless services.



Qualification Questions



The VA should learn to determine:

title: WordPress Developer (Bricks + ACF) for a Vacation Rental Marketing Agency (30-40 Hr, Long-Term)
description:
Hi! I'm Jim, and I run a small US marketing agency called Digital Redefined.



We work with vacation rental operators, the people who own and manage short-term rental properties, and we help them get guests to book directly with them instead of through Airbnb and VRBO. Our client sites run on WordPress with Bricks, ACF and our own booking plugin.



I'm looking for one developer to own the front-end work on those sites full-time, long-term.



THE WORK



- Building pages in Bricks and ACF on client websites, including a new kind of property page we've just launched. There's a written build guide for it, and it will be your first project.

- Our own agency website, which is built in Etch

- Looking after a small group of client sites: updates, maintenance and security, using MainWP, GridPane and Cloudflare

- SEO work: Rank Math, schema markup and fixing Google Search Console issues

-
 templates in Klaviyo, and website forms

- Everything gets built on staging first and checked there, then handed to me to sign off before it goes live



You'll build on top of our booking plugin, not inside it. Reading PHP is enough; you won't be writing plugins.



WHO I'M HOPING TO FIND



- You've built real sites in Bricks and ACF, and you can show me them. Tutorials and practice projects don't count.

- Experience with EtchWP is a bonus.

- You work staging first, production second, and you know why the order matters.

- You check your own work before you call it done, and you can tell me how you checked.

- You tell me how things are going without waiting to be asked.

- You write clear English. If something's wrong, you can explain it in a message without needing a call.

- Use AI tools as much as you like. I do. What matters is that you check what they give you and can explain it.  If brought on after a trial, you'll be provided a subscription.



Nice to have: MainWP or GridPane, Rank Math and schema, Search Console, Klaviyo, WS Form, Etch.



HOW I WORK



I don't micromanage, and I don't want to. Instead, I ask that you keep me in the loop.



If something's running late, or you're stuck, or a brief doesn't make sense, just tell me. I'd much rather hear about it on Wednesday than be surprised on Friday. Nobody here gets in trouble for raising a problem early. It's one of the things I value most in the people I work with, and I'll tell you when you do it.



When you tell me something is done, tell me what you checked. "Done, tested the booking form on mobile and desktop, both working" tells me far more than "Done."



You'll track your time per task in ClickUp. That's mostly so I can scope work properly: if something keeps taking twice as long as I expected, that's my estimate that needs fixing, not your speed.



THE DETAILS



- Full-time, 40 hours a week

- $1,400 to $1,800 per month

- Long-term. I'm hiring someone I hope will still be here in two years.

- Four hours a day overlapping US Eastern business hours, at a fixed time we agree on together (for example 8 AM to 12 PM Eastern, which is evening in the Philippines). You can arrange the rest of your hours.

- A short paid trial task first, at full rate, so we both find out if this fits

- A written agreement signed by both of us before you start



HOW TO APPLY



I read every application myself, and I'll reply to everyone who sends these four things:



1. Links to two or three sites you built in Bricks, and which parts of each were yours.



2. Which of these you've used, and for roughly how long: ACF, MainWP, GridPane, Rank Math, Klaviyo, Etch.



3. Short answers to these two questions, in your own words:



   "Tell me about a time you shipped something that broke. How did you find out?"



   "Tell me about something you built or changed that nobody asked you to."



   Everyone has a story for the first one. I'm not looking for a spotless record. I want to know how you found out and what you check now because of it.



4. Start your message with the word STAGING, so I know you read this far.



Looking forward to reading these.



— Jim

title: Senior Accountant / Controller (PTO, 13th Month, Bonuses)
description:
Most controller titles offered from the Philippines are a bookkeeping queue with a better name. This one is the real seat. You will be the financial authority for business groups with up to $30 million in revenue, and you will still do your own bank recs.



Who we are



We are a US accounting and tax firm. We have worked with business owners since 1991, and most of our accounting work is for multi-unit franchise groups: owners with ten, twenty or more stores, each in its own entity, closing on the franchise system's period calendar.



You would work directly with us. No agency in the middle, no account manager speaking for you, and nobody billing your hours to a client you are never allowed to talk to.



The seat



You are the controller for a group of our largest franchise clients. When an owner asks whether they can afford the next store, or what the bank will see in the covenant test, you are the person who knows. Not because you read a summary someone else prepared. Because you built the numbers.



What you own:



The close and the financial statements. Every period, on the franchise system's calendar, which for most of our clients means a 13-period year. Statements the owner can use, ready when promised.

Budgets and cash forecasts. You tell the owner what the next quarter looks like before it arrives.

Lender and covenant reporting. You run the covenant calculations and you know where each group stands against its loan terms before the bank does.

Internal controls. Over cash and payables, store by store. You find the gap before it becomes a loss.

Store purchases and sales. You read the closing documents, book the purchase price allocation, set up or retire the assets and intangibles, and produce the numbers a buyer or a lender will ask for.

The owner relationship. You are the owner's main financial contact. You explain the numbers on a call, plainly, and you send weekly reports to the clients who get them. Every week, without a reminder.



You still do the work



This is not an advisory role and it is not a management role. The person in this seat does bank reconciliations.

You reconcile the accounts yourself. Groups with dozens of bank accounts across dozens of entities. You find every difference and you prove it. You do not plug it, and you do not book a balancing entry to make it go away.

You book the hard entries yourself. Franchise fees and the intangibles they create, their amortization, and activity between related entities.

You review newer staff within 48 hours and send their work back with notes they can learn from.

You train. When a newer accountant asks how a client works, you show them that day.

You write it down. Every client you run has a current written procedure: how its bank feeds work and which entries are unusual to it.



If a controller title means you stopped touching reconciliations years ago, this is the wrong seat. We want someone who can explain a covenant test to an owner at ten in the morning and find a $312 difference in a bank rec at eleven.



The grunt work is going away. You help us retire it



We are rolling out AI tools over the coming months, and bank reconciliation matching is first on the list. The aim is to take the repetitive work off your desk so your hours go to the judgment calls.



You will help us test these tools on real clients. That means using them, telling us where they get things wrong, and checking every number they produce until we trust them. You do not need prior experience with AI. You need to want it, and you need to stay skeptical of it.



Hours



You work Philippine hours with a fixed overlap into the US Eastern morning, 7 to 11am Eastern. Owners call in that window and our team meets in it. We agree the rest of your day with you and then we keep to it.



Pay and Benefits



$4,500 USD per month

Plus 13th month pay. Uncommon in a contractor arrangement. We pay it anyway

Unlimited paid time off. The statutory floor in this country is five days a year. We do not count yours at all, and we expect you to spend it

Philippine daytime hours with one agreed US overlap window

Philippine public holidays observed. You work your country's calendar, not ours

Signing bonus to cover a second monitor, UPS, or generator

US CPA or EA sponsorship if you want it. We pay the fees and give you study time

That is the top of what this market pays a controller on US accounts, and we set it there on purpose. We want the best person available, and we do not want to lose them the moment somebody else makes an offer.



What you bring



At least eight years of accounting for US clients, with at least three of them owning the full close and financial reporting for a multi-entity group, as controller or in practice

Franchise or other multi-unit experience: many entities under one owner, with numbers that have to tie

Hands-on experience with store or business acquisitions and sales: closing documents, purchase price allocation, intangibles and amortization

Budgets, cash forecasts and loan covenant reporting you have built yourself

Bank reconciliations you have done yourself in the last twelve months

Experience reviewing other accountants' work and training newer staff

Thomson Reuters Accounting CS. If your command is in another professional package, say which and we will talk. QuickBooks Online and ShareFile are useful

A record of logging your time on every task, because some of our clients are billed on it

English strong enough to explain a set of financial statements to a US business owner on a live call

A stable home setup and the discipline to run your own day

A Philippine CPA or progress toward a US CPA is a plus. It is not required.



How we work



Read this part twice. We hire for it with the same weight as the technical skills above.

No task is beneath the seat. The controller does reconciliations. The title does not change that.

We change how we work, often. We are rebuilding the firm around automation, and processes that worked last year get replaced. When a new process arrives, you try it in good faith. If you think it is wrong, you say so in writing to the person who owns it, with your reasons, and then you follow the decision.

Your knowledge belongs on paper. Being the only person who knows how a client works is not job security here. It is a risk to the client, and we treat it as one.

Disagree with the work, never with the person. Problems go to the right person, privately, in a normal tone. We do not settle disagreements in the team chat.

You own your deadlines. If one is going to slip, you tell us before it slips, not after.

Verify, do not guess. A number you cannot support is not finished, however close the deadline is.



Your first 90 days



Days 1 to 30: You learn our systems and shadow the accountant who runs each client today through one full period close. By day 30 you have run one close yourself with review, bank recs included.

Days 31 to 60: You run your clients' closes and reconciliations yourself, weekly reports included. Every client you hold has a written procedure, written or updated by you. You have had a first financial review call with each owner.

Days 61 to 90: Each of your groups has a cash forecast and, where it has a loan, a covenant calculation you built. You are reviewing newer staff within 48 hours. You have tested our first AI reconciliation tool on at least one of your clients and told us what it gets wrong.



To apply

It takes about 20 minutes, and your answers are the first thing we read.

title: Organizational Rockstar Wanted — Help Us Make History!
description:
The Great History Challenge is a history competition for middle school (grades 6–8) students. We work with teachers across the US to give their students the opportunity to shine. We believe that by creating fun educational experiences, we can help students love learning!



We're a small, growing team that works hard, has fun, and genuinely cares about making a difference.



**THE GOAL**



We're looking for an **Executive Virtual Assistant** to become an important part of our team.



But we don't want just anyone...



We're looking for an organizational rockstar! Someone who loves turning chaos into order, gets satisfaction from crossing things off a to-do list, and takes pride in making sure nothing falls through the cracks.



Initially, a big part of your job will be helping our founder stay organized, focused, and productive. But that's just the beginning!



As you learn about our organization, we want you to take ownership of more projects and responsibilities. We're looking for someone who thinks ahead, takes initiative, and is excited to grow with us.



**ABOUT THE JOB**



This is a full-time, remote position working during US Eastern business hours (8 AM–5 PM).



Because we're a small team, you'll wear many hats. Here are some of the things you'll be doing:



- Help our founder plan and prioritize each day, keep track of commitments, and follow through on important projects

- Manage tasks and projects in ClickUp using the Getting Things Done (GTD) methodology

- Manage
 inboxes, calendars, scheduling, and follow-ups

- Help with sales and marketing administration, including
 campaigns, spreadsheets, contact lists, and mailings

- Take ownership of administrative projects and processes from beginning to end

- Identify opportunities to improve how we work and help make those improvements happen



We also want someone who will **help keep us accountable**. If we've agreed that something is important, we want you to help make sure it gets done—even if that means respectfully reminding the boss!



Don't worry if you don't know all our software tools right now. We're a team of former teachers, and we're happy to teach you what you need to know.



**ABOUT YOU**



- You are naturally organized and love keeping things running smoothly

- You take initiative rather than waiting for instructions

- You have excellent written and spoken English

- You are familiar with Getting Things Done (GTD), or excited to learn it

- You are curious, resourceful, and enjoy solving problems

- You take pride in your attention to detail and following through on commitments

- You are enthusiastic, positive, and eager to learn new skills

- You want to grow and take on more responsibility over time



**ABOUT US**



We're a small, friendly organization. We value good ideas, open communication, flexibility, a sense of humor, and people who genuinely care about their work.



**We believe in treating people like adults.** We don't believe in micromanaging or watching the clock. We trust our team members to do great work, communicate openly, and follow through on their commitments.



We also know that life happens! Family celebrations, appointments, and unexpected situations are part of life. We're happy to be flexible when you need it. All we ask is that you communicate with us and keep the team informed.



We love helping our team members grow, too! In fact, our previous Virtual Assistant has grown into a department leadership role—which is one of the reasons we're hiring now!



If you're looking for a place where you can make a difference, learn new things, and become an important part of a team, we'd love to meet you!



**COMPENSATION & SCHEDULE**



- Full-time, remote position

- $600–$800 USD per month, depending on experience

- 13th-month bonus

- Monday–Friday, 8 AM–5 PM US Eastern Time (Philippines night shift)

- Friendly, flexible, and supportive work environment with amble time off



We'll begin with a **30-day introductory evaluation period** to make sure we're a great fit for each other. Our hope is to find someone who will grow with us for years to come!



**HOW TO APPLY**



We'd love to hear from you!



Please apply directly through OnlineJobs.ph using the subject line:



**I can keep you organized**



In your application, please include:



1. A short introduction telling us a little about yourself and why this position interests you.

2. A link to one article, video, or other resource that you think would be helpful for someone trying to become more organized and productive.

3. Two or three sentences explaining why you chose that resource.



Please follow these instructions carefully. We will only review applications that include all three items.



We're not looking for a perfectly polished corporate cover letter. We want to get a sense of who you are, how you think, and what excites you!



We look forward to hearing from you!

title: Practice Marketing Project Manager (PH)
description:

Practice Marketing Project Manager (PH)

The Role

We're looking for a Practice Marketing Project Manager to give our Practice Marketing team the project management muscle it needs to grow. Right now, the team's own bandwidth is the ceiling on how many accounts we can service well — this role raises that ceiling.



You'll keep our top accounts on track, hold timelines and deliverables accountable, and free up our Practice Marketing Managers to spend their time on strategy and client relationships instead of chasing tasks. You'll also be stepping into the role of process-builder for the department — the systems and templates you create won't just serve today's accounts, they'll become the backbone the team scales on as Moxie takes on more clients.



This is a foundational hire for the team: half the job is running today's accounts cleanly, and half is building the infrastructure that lets Practice Marketing grow without sacrificing quality.





Our Objectives for the Role

- Bring full visibility to our top accounts by standing up a project tracking system and owning status reporting, so timelines, deliverables, and owners are always clear — without a manager needing to chase for updates

- Build and roll out a standardized project plan template that every new account runs on, so onboarding and delivery are consistent across the whole department

- Measurably improve delivery performance by reducing missed deadlines and late deliverables across top accounts, with a clear before-and-after tied to account retention

- Stand up a capacity planning process that shows the team's real workload, so leadership always knows when there's room to take on a new account

- Grow into a trusted operator who brings data-backed recommendations to leadership and takes on a piece of account load independently — positioning this role for growth into a Senior Project Manager or team lead track

- If things go even better than expected, you become the reason our top accounts run without fire drills — and the model we point to as we open new markets and bring on new clients.





We're Looking For

- A systems builder, not just a tracker. You don't just maintain a project tracker — you've built one from scratch, templated a process, or standardized a workflow that other people then adopted.

- Comfort owning accountability without owning the relationship. You can hold timelines and deliverables firm with marketing managers and clients without being the strategic or client-facing lead yourself.

- A bias toward visibility. You default to making status, risk, and ownership obvious to everyone — not just tracked in your own head or inbox.

- Judgment on when to flag versus when to solve. You can tell the difference between a risk that needs to be escalated now and one you can quietly resolve yourself.

- Early-career hunger for ownership. You want a role that stretches past "coordinate the calendar" and are motivated by building something that outlasts you.





Why Join Us?

- Above all, we're in this to empower small business owners to own and grow their businesses. If you succeed, MedSpas remain the opportunity for independent owner-operators instead of being dominated by a small number of large chains. If that speaks to you, speak to us.

- Real ownership, early. You won't be buried in busywork — you'll build the systems a growing marketing team runs on.

- Direct access to US-based leadership and clients, with your fingerprints on how Moxie scales.

- A clear growth path from Project Manager into a leadership track, with clear metrics to show your progress along the way.

- Competitive salary

title: Long Term CapCut Video Editor | YouTube + Social Media
description:
I’m a content creator and business owner looking for one video editor I can build a long term working relationship with.



Most of the time, I will provide the rough cut.



You will not usually be digging through hours of random footage trying to figure out what the video is supposed to be.



I handle the story and rough cut first. Your job is to take it from there and make the video feel finished, engaging, and visually interesting.



I create personality driven content around money, business, personal growth, relationships, lifestyle, and life in general.



The work will include both long form YouTube videos and short form content for Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts.





WHAT I’M LOOKING FOR



I want an editor who actually understands the content they are editing.



Someone who can recognize when a moment is funny, important, emotional, awkward, or worth letting breathe.



Someone who can look at a rough cut and think, “I know what would make this better,” without needing me to explain every single editing decision.



That might mean adding B roll, screenshots, text, memes, graphics, music, sound effects, zooms, or other creative elements.



It also means knowing when NOT to add something.



I do not want videos where something is flying onto the screen every three seconds just because you know how to do it.



Good pacing, storytelling, humor, personality, and visual taste matter more to me than flashy effects.



You do not need to be the most technically advanced editor in the world. I would rather work with someone who has strong creative instincts, communicates well, and can learn my style.





YOU SHOULD BE COMFORTABLE WITH



CapCut Desktop



Talking head and personality driven content



Long form and short form editing



Adding relevant B roll and visual elements



Working with spoken English content



Making creative decisions independently



Receiving feedback and applying what you learn to future videos



I specifically want to work in CapCut so we can share project files and I can easily review the timeline or make small changes myself when needed.





HOURS, PAY, AND GROWTH



This role will start at approximately 10 hours per week.



Pay is up to $10 USD per hour, depending on your skill, experience, editing quality, and speed.



I am looking for someone I can work with long term, so there will also be opportunities for:



Performance bonuses when videos perform especially well



Raises over time as you learn my style, consistently deliver strong work, and take on more responsibility



Additional hours as my content output and business grow



I want the person editing my content to benefit when the content is winning too.





THE GOAL



I do not want to hire a different freelancer every few videos.



I want one editor who gets to know me, my sense of humor, my content, and my editing style.



You will have references and feedback while you learn what I like, but the goal is for you to become more independent over time and make strong creative decisions without waiting for instructions on every detail.





TO APPLY



Please send:



1. Three videos you personally edited that you think are the best match for this role. Please choose your three most relevant examples instead of sending your entire portfolio.



2. Confirm that you currently edit in CapCut Desktop.



3. Your normal hourly rate in USD.



4. Your current weekly availability.



5. Tell me which of the three videos you submitted is your favorite and why.



Start your application with the word STORY so I know you read the full post.



That’s it.



I will review your actual editing work first.



If your work looks like it could be a good fit, I will invite you to complete a small paid editing trial using my actual footage.

title: Publicity / PR Consultant
description:
About the role



Vanderburgh Sober Living (VSL) equips and supports the owner-operators who open and run recovery homes, and is the largest network of Level II recovery residences in the United States. VSL is affiliated with the Vanderburgh Foundation, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit. We are hiring a part-time Publicity / PR Consultant to get VSL featured in local news, national news, and trade publications in our field. The focus of this role is earned press and trade media coverage: news stories, articles, interviews, and features. This is not an advertising or paid-placement role. Your job is to build relationships with journalists and editors and to turn VSL's work into published coverage.



What you will do

 marketing platforms

WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR

title: Creative Manager (WordPress, Shopify, HTML/CSS)
description:
We’re a U.S.-based consulting and technology company with an international team. We build and manage websites, apps, digital products, and brands for clients across many industries.

We’re looking for a Creative Manager / Web Designer who can lead the creative direction of digital projects while also being hands-on with execution.



This is not a junior role and not a social media position.



We’re looking for someone with a strong design eye who can take a project from an idea or brief to a polished, professional digital experience. You should be comfortable creating mockups, developing visual direction, working with developers, and being hands-on with WordPress when needed.



You don’t need to be a full-time developer. Strong design and creative thinking come first.



What You’ll Do



Lead the visual and creative direction of website and software projects

Translate briefs and ideas into clear visual concepts, layouts, and mockups

Create website designs that are clean, modern, professional, and user-focused

Develop page layouts and design systems rather than relying solely on pre-built templates

Design website interfaces and user experiences with attention to usability and conversion

Customize themes, layouts, and page-builder components when needed

Work closely with developers and internal teams to bring designs to life

Review completed work and ensure the final product matches the intended design

Identify design, layout, UX, and usability issues and propose solutions

Manage multiple creative projects and keep work moving toward deadlines

Communicate directly with internal teams and, when needed, clients





Required Skills



Strong background in web and digital design

Excellent eye for layout, typography, spacing, hierarchy, color, and visual consistency

Experience designing websites from scratch or through custom mockups

Strong WordPress experience, including themes, page builders, plugins, and customization

Good understanding of UX/UI principles and responsive design

Ability to turn a brief or rough idea into a clear visual direction

Ability to manage multiple projects independently

Strong written English and communication skills

A portfolio that demonstrates actual website and digital product design work





Nice to Have



Figma or similar design/prototyping tools

JavaScript knowledge

Experience working with developers

Experience managing designers or creative teams

SEO and website performance knowledge

Experience designing web applications or software interfaces

Branding and visual identity experience





What We’re Looking For

We’re looking for someone who can look at a blank page and know how to turn it into something good.



You should be able to:



Take a vague idea and develop a creative direction

Create mockups before jumping into a template

Explain why a design works, not just make something look nice

Recognize when a website feels dated, cluttered, inconsistent, or poorly structured

Balance aesthetics with usability and business objectives

Work independently and make thoughtful creative decisions

Collaborate with developers without needing to be a developer yourself

Take ownership of a project from concept through completion





This Role Is NOT For You If



Your experience is primarily social media graphics or Canva

You primarily work from pre-built templates without developing your own design direction

You consider yourself a developer first and have limited experience with visual design

You need detailed instructions for every step of a project

You’re looking for a short-term freelance gig

You’re not comfortable taking ownership of creative decisions





What We Value

Design thinking. Ownership. Initiative. Attention to detail.



We want someone who doesn't just execute instructions, but can look at a project and say, “Here's how I think we should approach this."



Technical skills are valuable, but your ability to think creatively, solve design problems, and produce strong digital experiences is what matters most.



How to Apply

Please include:



Your resume

Your portfolio

Examples of websites or digital products you have designed

A brief explanation of your role in those projects





Please do not submit a portfolio consisting primarily of social media graphics or Canva templates. We are specifically looking for strong web and digital design work.

title: ShipBob Logistics & Fulfillment Specialist – E-commerce
description:

Excellent written and verbal English

Bonuses and raises based on quality work and performance!

About Inner Create

Inner Create is an established Architectural Consultancy in the UK, celebrating a decade of excellence in 3D modeling, energy assessments, and project management. Visual Aesthetic: Manage the "look and feel" of the brand. Whether it’s a PDF brochure, a social post, or a website update, it must meet high architectural design standards.



Human-Centric Writing: Produce long-form blogs and case studies that feel authentic and expert. You must be able to write in a nuanced, professional British English tone that builds deep trust with local homeowners and developers.



Portfolio Presentation: Use Elementor and WordPress to showcase our projects, ensuring layouts are clean, modern, and visually impactful.



3. CRM & Local Lead Nurturing (GoHighLevel)



Pipeline Ownership: Manage GoHighLevel to ensure local leads are nurtured through intelligent, well-timed automations.



Local Authority: Tailor email campaigns to reflect local UK market trends, building Inner Create’s reputation as the "go-to" local expert.



Requirements

Strategic Mindset: Proven experience in creating and executing a marketing plan from scratch.



The "Design Eye": A portfolio that demonstrates a clean, high-end, and professional aesthetic (experience with luxury or technical brands is a plus).



Expert Copywriting: Exceptional command of British English. You can write content that feels "human" and expert, knowing when to use AI for efficiency and when to write by hand for authenticity.



Tech Stack: Proficiency in GoHighLevel, WordPress/Elementor, and Canva/Adobe Suite.



Self-Starter: You don’t wait for a task list; you see a gap and suggest a solution.

title: Paid Media Specialist (Performance Marketing)
description:
Starting USD $1,000 - $1,400 / month | Full-time | Remote | Fast-track hiring | Hire by Oct 23| Asia Time Zone



Are you a performance marketer who knows why the numbers moved, not just what they are?



Apply below to own real ad channels across Meta, TikTok, Google and more — with stable clients and active coaching in AI workflows.







---



[1] About Ally



Ally helps founders and leaders scale themselves before they scale their companies.



Founded by leaders who have scaled and operated 8-figure+ businesses, we partner with top operators and support clients including a NASDAQ-listed company.



We match Executive Partners (EPs) with fast-growing e-commerce and creative businesses to bring structure, clarity, and execution leverage — blending human judgment with modern AI systems.



We're not a traditional VA agency. We're a modern operating partner helping global teams run smarter and faster.



This role sits with one of our clients — a team that took a consumer health brand from zero to $100M USD. Built by operators who previously scaled a NASDAQ-listed company, Casetify, and Peak21, the brand crossed 8-figure revenue and 1M+ customers in under 36 months. You would work inside their marketing team, with Ally behind you.



---



[2] The Role



This is a high-caliber, high-growth marketing team with ambitions to scale significantly further. They are adding paid media capacity — not to maintain what is running, but to push harder on what is already working and open up what is next.



As an Executive Partner in paid media, you will own the performance of the ad channels we give you. You buy the media, watch the numbers every day, and tell the team what they mean and what to do next.



Leadership does not open the ad platforms. They read your report. That means your report has to be right every single day, and it has to come with a point of view, not just a set of figures.



For your first month or two you will bring your recommendations to the marketing lead for approval. Once you have shown you can read the numbers, you optimise on your own.



---



[3] What You'll Do



What you own:



- How your channels perform. Keep the channels assigned to you running, and grow them. That means managing the spend, creating and managing the ad accounts, setting up a replacement when one gets rejected, and flagging billing before a lapse stops our campaigns.

- The daily report. Build and maintain it across every funnel, and know why each formula works rather than just where to type the number. Leadership never opens the ad platforms, they read your report. It has to be right every day.

- How the agency content performs. Several agencies produce and post content for us. You get it live as ads on time, and you own how it does once it is running.

- Keeping the accounts alive. Our product category is high risk for ad and account bans. Monitor policy changes, spot the risk early, and act before a channel gets disrupted.

- Spotting things first. Flag underperformance, anomalies or opportunities before anyone asks.



What you work out:



- Analyze the data. Not just what happened, but why, and what to do next.

- Analyze creatives against performance and say what we should make more of.

- Research what is working for other brands and competitors. Not just ads: landing pages, messaging, offers and campaign strategies. Bring back specific things we should test, and draft the advertorials yourself (AI tools welcome).

- Look beyond your own assignment. Check what is happening on the other channels so you understand the whole picture.



What you run day to day:



- Launch ads at volume across Meta, TikTok, Snapchat, Reddit, Taboola and Google. Several hundred a week, mostly through bulk tools rather than one at a time.

- Work with our internal creative team and our external agencies on what is coming and when.

- Work directly with platform reps on rejections, approvals and questions.



---



[4] What Success Looks Like at 90 Days



- Your channels are growing. Spend and revenue up, ROAS held at target.

- You have a repeatable way to test creatives, and you are consistently finding and scaling the winners.

- Nothing has stopped. No campaign down because of a billing lapse, a rejected account, or a policy change you did not see coming.

- Your reports are trusted. Leadership d
 off them without going to check the platforms.

- You are bringing ideas, not just numbers. Things you found working for other brands that we should be testing.



---



[5] What We're Looking For



- You understand how paid ads work on at least one platform. Not just uploading. You know what to check, what to look at, and why. This is the one thing we cannot train from zero.

- Initiative. You see what needs doing and you do it. We can tell within a week who has this and who does not.

- You ask questions constantly. We would rather you ask ten times a day than stay quiet and hand in a report with mistakes in it.

- You treat the work as yours. The people who do well here push on something because they spotted the opportunity, not because someone asked them to.

- Strong attention to detail — accuracy in the data, polish in the presentation.

- Able to present data clearly — formatting, structure and visual clarity matter.

- Open to working on any platform — Meta, TikTok, Snapchat, Reddit, Taboola, Google. You may be strongest on one, but you will not get to stay there.

- Comfortable with bulk launch tooling like AdManage or Revealbot, or able to pick it up fast.

- Comfortable with spreadsheets, dashboards, and numbers.

- Familiarity with Google Sheets or Excel.

- Has used AI tools in their workflow (preferred, not required).

- Agency or in-house media buying experience is a plus. Time served matters less than knowing what you are looking at.



One thing this role is not: you will not be designing creatives. Our internal team and our agencies produce the assets. You shape what they make by telling them what the data says is working, and you will write advertorials yourself.



If you have read this far: open your video by naming which of our six platforms you have actually run ads on, and which you have never touched. Be honest. Nobody has all six, and we would rather know now.



---



[6] Schedule



5 days a week, 8am to 5pm Philippine time. Your two days off include one weekday, so one of your five working days falls on a weekend and the team always has coverage. We will confirm which days when we assign your channels.



If we ask you to cover a sixth day, that is overtime.



---



[7] What You'll Get



- Attractive starting rate and grow fast — starting at USD $1,000 - $1,400 / month

- Two weeks of one-on-one walkthrough training with the marketing lead

- Paid subscriptions to the tools you need

- Direct access to global founders and operators

- Mentorship and clear growth paths

- Real spend across six platforms on a brand that is scaling. That is a track record you can point at later.

- Fully remote setup

- Asia Time Zone

- Work that truly matters — every report you build drives real revenue decisions for global brands



---



[8] HOW TO APPLY



Submit your application here:

- Your relevant paid media or marketing experience

In the video, also answer this:



Last 7 days, three ads:



- Ad A: $120 spent, 1 purchase, $95 revenue

- Ad B: $2,400 spent, 41 purchases, $4,300 revenue

Which one would you scale, and why? A minute is plenty. We are listening for how you think, not how polished you are. It is the main thing we shortlist on.



Applications sent outside this link will not be reviewed.

[9] OTHER OPEN POSITIONS AT ALLY

title: Technical QA Engineer (Laravel + Vue 2, post-deploy), EU property-tech + SaaS, remote
description:
Role

We ship small changes to our live platforms often. We want a technical QA engineer with a real developer background: you think like a user, but you can also read the code path, review merge requests, and tell us when the fix or the AI-suggested change should be different. After each release you check that landlords, renters, candidates and companies can still get from A to B to C. You are not the person who builds features full time, but you are close to a half-developer on our stack. Speed and quality, not one at the cost of the other.



About us

We are a European property-tech company. We run several live rental and property platforms on one shared Laravel and Vue 2 codebase, plus a recruitment SaaS where candidates record video intakes for companies and agencies. We use GitLab merge requests. We care about security, privacy, and small reviewable changes.



Where you sit in our flow

We roll out to production often and we want to keep that pace. Developers deploy; you are not a gate before release and you do not own the deploy button. After each production rollout you test on
 the journeys that release touched, then the critical paths users depend on, on desktop and mobile, with test accounts and safe paths where we need them. You are the second check after go-live, not a blocker in front of it. When something fails for a real user, you report it fast with steps, expected versus actual, and enough detail that a developer can fix it the same day.



How we work

Our developers work with AI coding assistants and keep their changes small. You test the outcome in the browser and you sanity-check the change in GitLab: read the diff, spot risky patterns, and push back when generated code is sloppy or the wrong layer was touched. If something works on paper but feels wrong in the browser, you say so. You may use AI tools yourself, but the pass or fail comes from what you verified, not from what the model claimed.



What you will do

- After each production rollout, smoke-test the journeys that release touched, on desktop and on mobile

- Re-run the critical journeys per product: listing a property, booking a viewing, uploading documents, recording a video intake, reviewing candidates

- Explore beyond the release note when something looks fragile

- Check that a change on one platform did not break or leak into another platform on the same codebase

- Write clear bug reports: steps to reproduce, expected versus actual, severity, environment, browser and device, screenshot or short video

- Point developers to the file, layer, or request: Blade, Vue component, controller, query, or API response

- Give UX feedback in plain words, for example "a landlord would not know what to do here"

- Review merge requests and recent commits: what changed, what could regress, what should have been tested, what you would do differently

- Suggest concrete improvements to developers (and to AI-generated patches): safer query, clearer validation, better error handling, smaller scope



Requirements

- Strong technical background: you have worked as a developer or as QA embedded with developers, and you can read Laravel and Vue 2 code in a real codebase, not only tutorials

- Hands-on experience with Laravel web applications and Vue 2 front ends in production, or equivalent depth with a similar PHP plus SPA stack and a clear plan to work in our Vue 2 patterns

- Experience with multi-brand or multi-tenant products: one codebase, several sites or customers, and you know how a fix on one brand can break another

- Proven QA on live web products, with examples where your report or your review caught something others missed

- You think in user journeys and in the people behind them

- Clear written English, short and precise

- Solid GitLab or GitHub habits: branches, merge requests, reading diffs, commenting on specific lines

- Browser developer tools: console, network tab, status codes; you tie UI symptoms to backend responses

- Comfortable challenging AI-assisted development: you review output like a senior teammate, not like a checklist-only tester

- Reliable and self-directed: you find the next useful check without being told

- This role is QA and review first. We do not hire you primarily to ship features. Occasional tiny fixes are a bonus, not the job description.



Nice to have

- Accessibility basics: keyboard use, contrast, readable forms

- Ideas for light automated checks or regression notes, without making automation the whole role

- Docker-based local setup or Laravel Mix familiarity



Working hours: full time, 40 hours a week, Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 17:00 Amsterdam time. That is 15:00 to 23:00 in the Philippines in European summer, and 16:00 to 00:00 when Europe switches to winter time. Please state your timezone and the window you can reliably cover each workday.



Paid trial (before full engagement)

A paid trial week of about five working days, full time, at $3 per hour, tracked with TimeProof after signing. We give you test accounts, a short list of recent rollouts to verify the same way you would after go-live, and read-only visibility on merge requests where useful. You test like a real user on desktop and mobile, file bug reports and UX notes, and add technical review comments where you see risk in the change. You may use AI tools, but you must not paste secrets, customer data, production logs, or private business information into external tools. You must be able to explain and defend everything you report and every review comment.



The deal

Remote, full time, long term. Hours are tracked with TimeProof. Rate: $3 per hour to start, reviewed on quality and impact. This is a long-term role, not a one-off project.



How to apply (English, no template letters)

1) Start your message with ABC.

2) One bug you found in production that others missed: how you reproduced it and how you reported it.

3) How you would test a release right after it goes live, without slowing every release down.

4) One example of UX feedback you gave that changed a flow.

5) A form submits and nothing happens. What do you send the developer?

6) One merge request or diff you reviewed: what you looked at in the code, what you worried about, and what you asked the developer to change.

7) Your timezone and the Amsterdam-time window you can cover.



Keep it short. Selected applicants do a short video intake on our platform before we talk.



Do not apply if

- You are not the person who will do the work

- You only know QA in theory and cannot give real examples

- You have never read application code or merge request diffs in a real job

- You only write automated tests and do not think about the people using the product

- You want a pure development role with no testing responsibility

- You cannot write clear English

- You would paste secrets, production logs, or customer data into external tools

title: Financial & Revenue Performance Analyst  | Long-Term Opportunity | European Health & Beauty Business
description:
Part-Time Financial & Revenue Performance Analyst (FP&A / Power BI)



Initial 40-Hour Project | 3 - 5 Hours/Week Ongoing | Long-Term Opportunity | European Health & Beauty Business



We are looking for a highly capable, analytical and commercially minded Financial & Revenue Performance Analyst to support a growing premium health, beauty and wellness company based in Iceland.



This is not a bookkeeping, accounting or general virtual assistant role.



We are looking for someone who is highly confident in Power BI, Excel, financial analysis, budgeting, forecasting and business performance reporting.



You should enjoy working with numbers, understanding how a business operates, identifying financial risks and opportunities, and turning data into clear, actionable recommendations.



You will work directly with the Founder/CEO, but the goal is not for you to wait for daily instructions.



We want someone who can gradually take ownership of our financial and operational performance monitoring, identify trends and potential problems early, and proactively recommend ways to improve revenue, profitability, cost efficiency and cash flow.



What You’ll Be Responsible For



Financial Planning, Budgeting & Forecasting



* Build and maintain our annual financial budget, broken down by month

* Forecast revenue, operating expenses, profitability and cash requirements

* Compare actual financial performance against budgets and targets

* Analyse monthly and year-to-date variances

* Explain why results are above or below expectations

* Maintain a rolling forecast for the remainder of the financial year

* Identify potential financial risks before they become problems

* Recommend corrective actions when the business is not on track to meet its targets



Cash Flow Monitoring & Forecasting



* Build and maintain a rolling 13-week cash-flow forecast

* Monitor expected cash inflows and outflows

* Identify potential cash shortages in advance

* Analyse how changes in revenue, expenses and payment timing affect cash flow

* Monitor progress against cash reserve targets

* Recommend practical actions to strengthen liquidity and cash generation

* Provide clear early warnings when action may be required



Cost Analysis & Expense Optimisation



* Review operating expenses and recurring subscriptions

* Identify unused software, unnecessary costs and duplicated services

* Analyse spending trends and unusual cost increases

* Compare actual expenses against budget

* Identify opportunities to reduce costs without negatively affecting operations

* Evaluate the potential financial impact of proposed savings

* Track whether approved cost-saving measures deliver the expected results



Revenue Performance & Growth Opportunities



* Analyse revenue trends by month, treatment category and service

* Monitor average sales value and revenue per client

* Identify opportunities to increase revenue from existing clients and services

* Evaluate potential pricing changes and their financial impact

* Analyse treatment packages, pricing structures and revenue opportunities

* Model different revenue scenarios and their expected financial outcomes

* Identify underperforming services and opportunities to improve profitability

* Proactively recommend practical ways to increase recurring revenue and overall business performance



We want someone who can say:



“If we increase the price of this treatment by a small amount, based on current sales volume, here is the potential monthly and annual financial impact.”



Or:



“Based on current trends, we may fall below next month’s revenue target. Here is the estimated gap and what I recommend we do.”



Capacity, Booking Utilisation & Revenue Forecasting



We operate a treatment-based clinic where revenue is closely connected to booking capacity and utilisation.



You will help us understand how effectively we are using our available capacity.



Responsibilities include:



* Monitor current treatment booking utilisation

* Analyse available treatment capacity versus booked appointments

* Forecast expected utilisation and revenue for the coming weeks and months

* Identify periods with low booking demand or underutilised capacity

* Identify situations where additional staff availability may be needed

* Analyse revenue generated per treatment and per booked hour

* Evaluate how improvements in utilisation could affect revenue and profitability

* Recommend when operational or sales actions may be required to improve performance



The goal is to identify opportunities and risks early, rather than reacting after the month has already ended.



Sales Performance & Treatment Profitability



* Analyse average transaction value and average revenue per client

* Calculate average realised revenue per treatment

* Analyse direct treatment costs where data is available

* Evaluate contribution margins across different treatment categories

* Identify which treatments generate the strongest financial returns

* Analyse revenue and contribution per treatment hour

* Evaluate the profitability of different pricing and package structures

* Identify opportunities to improve revenue without unnecessarily increasing operating costs



You should understand the difference between selling a prepaid treatment package, receiving cash and delivering the treatments over time.



Power BI Dashboards & Reporting



Strong hands-on Power BI experience is an essential requirement for this position.



You will be responsible for building and maintaining clear, practical dashboards that help management understand business performance.



This includes:



* Build and maintain interactive Power BI dashboards

* Import, clean and transform data using Power Query

* Create reliable data models and relationships

* Build DAX measures and financial KPIs

* Develop dashboards for revenue, expenses, profitability, cash flow, sales and utilisation

* Compare actual performance against budgets and forecasts

* Create clear visual indicators for trends, variances and potential risks

* Establish repeatable data refresh and reporting processes

* Document data sources, calculations and dashboard maintenance procedures

* Continuously improve reporting accuracy, clarity and usefulness



We are not looking for dashboards that simply look impressive.



We want dashboards that help us make better business decisions.



Proactive Financial Monitoring & Recommendations



One of the most important parts of this role is identifying what management needs to know before being asked.



You will be expected to:



* Monitor agreed financial and operational KPIs

* Identify significant changes or concerning trends

* Highlight risks to revenue, profitability and cash flow

* Investigate unexpected results

* Prepare concise explanations and recommended next steps

* Prioritise recommendations based on their likely financial impact

* Follow up on approved improvements and measure their results



We want someone who can say:



“I noticed this is not performing as expected. Here is what I found, what it means financially, and what I recommend we do next.”



Rather than simply waiting to be told what to analyse.



Initial Project — First Two Weeks



The position begins with an approximately 40-hour paid setup and analysis project, ideally completed within two weeks.



The purpose of this initial project is to establish a practical financial and operational performance monitoring system.



This will include:



* Reviewing available financial and operational data

* Analysing historical revenue and operating expenses

* Identifying initial cost-saving opportunities

* Establishing a monthly annual budget and forecast

* Building a rolling 13-week cash-flow forecast

* Creating an initial capacity and utilisation forecasting model

* Establishing key revenue, sales and profitability metrics

* Building the first functional Power BI management dashboard

* Preparing an initial financial performance report

* Presenting key findings, risks, opportunities and recommended actions

* Documenting the ongoing reporting and monitoring process



The goal is to create a reliable, usable first version of the system, not to spend unnecessary time building something overly complicated.



More advanced automation or additional analysis can be developed later if justified.



Successful completion of the initial project may lead to an ongoing part-time position.



Ongoing Responsibilities



After the initial setup, the role will focus on maintaining the system and providing regular financial and operational insights.



Weekly:



* Update cash-flow and short-term revenue forecasts

* Monitor upcoming booking utilisation

* Identify important risks, variances and opportunities

* Flag issues requiring management attention



Monthly:



* Update financial dashboards and management reports

* Compare actual performance against budget

* Review revenue, costs, profitability and cash generation

* Update forecasts for the remaining year

* Review cost-saving and revenue improvement opportunities

* Present a concise summary of findings and recommended actions



We value clear conclusions and useful recommendations over lengthy reports.



The Person We Are Looking For



You may be a strong fit if you:



* Have proven experience in financial planning and analysis (FP&A)

* Have strong, practical experience with Microsoft Power BI

* Are highly proficient in Excel or Google Sheets

* Can independently build budgets and financial forecasts

* Understand cash-flow forecasting and financial performance analysis

* Are comfortable analysing revenue, expenses and profitability

* Have experience creating financial dashboards and KPI reports

* Understand data modelling, Power Query and DAX

* Can work with data from different business systems

* Have strong analytical and problem-solving skills

* Understand the commercial impact behind financial numbers

* Have excellent written English

* Have exceptional attention to detail

* Can work independently with minimal supervision

* Are proactive, reliable and highly organised

* Can explain complex financial information in simple, practical language

* Naturally look for ways to improve business performance



Experience with service-based businesses, clinics, wellness businesses or appointment-based operations is a strong advantage.



Experience with Shopify, booking systems or financial reporting automation is also an advantage.



Most importantly, we want someone who thinks beyond the spreadsheet.



Someone who understands that the purpose of financial analysis is not simply to report what happened, but to help the business make better decisions about what happens next.



How We Work



We use Notion as our central operating system.



Your tasks, projects, deadlines, documentation and time tracking will be managed there.



Financial models and reporting may be maintained in Excel or Google Sheets, with Power BI used as our primary management dashboard.



We believe in clear ownership, reliable reporting and proactive communication.



For recurring responsibilities, the goal is that you know what needs to be reviewed, when it needs to be updated and what good performance looks like without the CEO having to assign every individual task.



We also value documentation.



If something becomes recurring, we want to turn it into a repeatable process, template, checklist or automation.



The objective is to make our financial reporting more accurate, efficient and increasingly independent of the Founder/CEO.



About The House of Beauty



The House of Beauty is a premium, multi-award-winning health, wellness and non-invasive body clinic based in Reykjavík, Iceland.



We have been operating for 8+ years and have delivered 50,000+ treatments.



Our clients are primarily women, and our brand combines premium client experience with specialist expertise, technology and results-focused treatments.



We are now strengthening the financial and operational systems behind the business to support more predictable revenue, stronger profitability, improved cash flow and sustainable long-term growth.



Hours & Compensation



* Initial paid project: approximately 40 hours over two weeks

* Ongoing workload: approximately 3 hours per week / 12 hours per month

* $8–12 USD/hour, depending on experience and demonstrated capabilities

* Long-term opportunity for the right person

* Fully remote position

* Paid hourly with time tracking

* Initial 3-month probationary period for the ongoing role

* Additional hours only by prior agreement



We care more about accuracy, commercial insight, ownership and results than simply logging hours.



How to Apply



Please include the following in your application:



1. Start your application with the words: “THOB Finance”



This helps us confirm that you read the full job description.



2. Tell us about your experience with:



* Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A)

* Power BI

* Excel / Google Sheets

* Budgeting & Forecasting

* Cash Flow Forecasting

* Financial Dashboards & KPI Reporting



3. Rate yourself from 1–10 in each of those six areas.



4. Give us one real example of a financial dashboard, forecast or reporting system you personally built or significantly improved.



Explain:



* What was the business problem?

* What data sources did you work with?

* What did you personally build or analyse?

* What was the result or business impact?



5. Imagine you join us and discover that our revenue is 15% below budget, while operating expenses are 10% above budget.



What would you investigate first, and what information would you need before recommending actions?



6. Imagine that our treatment booking utilisation is significantly below target for next month.



How would you analyse the situation and identify opportunities to improve revenue?



7. Please describe your Power BI experience.



Include examples of dashboards you have personally built, your experience with Power Query and DAX, and how you have handled data refreshes.



8. How many hours per week are you currently committed to other clients or employment?



9. What is your current working schedule and timezone?



10. What is your expected hourly rate in USD?



11. Please include links, screenshots or examples of relevant Power BI dashboards, financial models or reports where possible.



Please remove any confidential client or employer information before sharing examples.



Shortlisted candidates will be invited to an interview.

title: Group Bookkeeper
description:
Key responsibilities:



Bookkeeping and close

• Process all purchase and sales invoices for four entities, assigning every cost and revenue line to the entity that economically carries it.

• Run the month-end close per entity: accruals, prepayments, depreciation of the station and power bank fleet, GL reconciliation.

• Maintain clean AR/AP ledgers, chase missing invoices and receipts, and keep a complete audit trail.

• Process expense reimbursements and kilometre declarations against policy.



Cash, payments and reconciliation

• Reconcile Stripe payouts, fees and refunds daily/weekly to the correct entity, in UTC with CET normalisation.

• Reconcile Airwallex (HK entities, multi-currency) and ABN AMRO/Revolut/bunq (NL entities) monthly, using account statements and MT940 exports.

• Prepare payment runs and maintain a 14-day payment overview per entity.



Intercompany

• Book and invoice monthly intercompany recharges (payroll cost allocation, management fees, licence/royalty fees, product mark-up).

• Keep current-account (rekening-courant) and loan balances between entities reconciled and agreed every month, including interest accruals.

• Maintain the supporting schedules finance and tax advisers need for transfer-pricing documentation.



Settlements and commissions

• Produce dealer settlements and venue/partner commission statements (self-billing) from platform data, reconciled to Stripe before they go out.

• Flag any gap between portal, Stripe and settlement figures before booking, not after.



Tax and compliance

• Prepare NL VAT returns and ICP listings for both B.V.s, including reverse-charge on non-EU (e.g. US SaaS) suppliers and intra-Community supplies to EU dealers.

• Prepare payroll journals from Nmbrs and track loonheffing payments and assessments.

• Support the HK annual audit, profits tax filings and Business Registration renewals together with the company secretary.

• Prepare year-end files for the NL accountant (jaarrekening, VPB) and the HK auditor.

• Escalate any VAT or cross-entity question to the external accountant for sign-off; you prepare, they confirm.



Systems and reporting

• Help migrate bookkeeping from Exact Online to Odoo (chart of accounts, VAT codes, entity setup, bank feeds).

• Deliver monthly management accounts input per entity (P&L, balance sheet, cash) and an NL vs. HQ split for Finance.

• Document every recurring process as an SOP and automate wherever the volume justifies it.



Must have:

• A bachelor's degree or other higher education in accounting, finance or a related field; a professional accounting qualification (e.g. CPA, ACCA, CMA) is a plus.

• 5+ years of hands-on bookkeeping, including multi-entity groups with intercompany flows.

• Solid working knowledge of EU VAT mechanics (returns, reverse charge, intra-Community supplies); hands-on Dutch VAT and ICP experience is a strong plus.

• Experience running a monthly close independently, end to end.

• Fluent English, written and spoken; able to read Dutch invoices and statements (tools like translation software are fine).

• Comfortable with Exact Online or a similar package, and strong in Excel/Google Sheets.



Nice to have

• Experience serving European clients remotely, as an independent freelancer.

• Experience with Hong Kong entities (audit cycle, profits tax, company secretary) or other non-EU group companies.

• Odoo accounting, ideally a migration.

• Payment-platform reconciliation (Stripe, Adyen, Airwallex) at high transaction volume.

• Startup or scale-up background: you build the process while running it.

• Familiarity with transfer-pricing documentation and royalty/licence flows.



How you work

• You own the outcome and flag problems early, with a proposed fix.

• You document what you do so it can be checked, repeated and automated.

• You know where your expertise ends and when to bring in the accountant.



Tools: Exact Online (moving to Odoo), Stripe, Airwallex, ABN AMRO, Revolut, Nmbrs, Google Workspace, Slack, 



Hours: Full-time (40 hrs/week)

Contract: Independent contractor (no agencies or BPO providers)

Location: Fully remote with CET business hours

Compensation: Hourly rate [TBD — in EUR or USD], invoiced monthly

Start date: [TBD]

title: Group Controller
description:
Key responsibilities:



Close and reporting

• Own the monthly close for all four entities and deliver it within 10 working days, with a documented close checklist.

• Produce monthly management accounts per entity (P&L, balance sheet, cash flow) and a consolidated group view, including a clear NL vs. HQ split.

• Prepare the monthly investor pack inputs: revenue by country and dealer, gross margin, burn rate, runway, cash position, EBITDA.

• Explain variances: budget vs. actual, month vs. month, with the drivers behind them.



Revenue and settlement control

• Own revenue recognition: platform data, Stripe and the ledger must agree before anything is booked.

• Review dealer settlements and venue/partner commission statements before they go out, and fix root causes when sources disagree.

• Define and maintain the policies behind settlements (e.g. treatment of refunds, non-return fees, adjustments).



Cash and planning

• Maintain a rolling 13-week cash flow forecast and the monthly liquidity plan per entity.

• Update the annual budget and rolling forecast together with the finance lead.

• Monitor payments due and working capital (AR/AP ageing) and flag risks early.



Intercompany and tax

• Own the intercompany framework: payroll cost allocation, management fees, licence/royalty fees, product mark-up, loans and current accounts, reconciled and agreed every month.

• Maintain the schedules needed for transfer-pricing documentation.

• Review NL VAT returns and ICP listings, reverse-charge and intra-Community treatment before filing.

• Coordinate the NL year-end (jaarrekening, VPB) with the external accountant and the HK audit and profits tax with the auditor and company secretary.

• Escalate any VAT or cross-entity question to the external accountant for sign-off; you prepare and review, they confirm.



Bookkeeping (hands-on, decreasing over time)

• Process invoices, bank, Stripe and Airwallex reconciliations, payroll journals and accruals while no separate bookkeeper is in place.

• Write the SOPs that allow this work to be handed to a bookkeeper later, and review that work once it is.



Controls, systems and fixed assets

• Set up and maintain internal controls: approval flows, segregation of duties, reconciliation sign-offs, audit trail.

• Lead the finance side of the Exact Online to Odoo migration: chart of accounts, VAT codes, entity setup, bank feeds, reporting.

• Own the fixed-asset register for the station and power bank fleet and its depreciation.

• Automate recurring work wherever the volume justifies it.



Must have:

• A bachelor's degree or other higher education in accounting, finance or a related field.

• 7+ years in accounting and finance, of which at least 3 in a controller or senior accountant role.

• Experience owning the close and management reporting for a multi-entity group with intercompany flows and consolidation.

• Solid working knowledge of EU VAT mechanics (returns, reverse charge, intra-Community supplies).

• Strong financial modelling in Excel/Google Sheets: cash flow forecasts, budgets, variance analysis.

• Fluent English, written and spoken; able to read Dutch invoices and statements (translation tools are fine).

• Willing and able to do hands-on bookkeeping alongside the controlling work.



Nice to have

• A professional accounting qualification (e.g. CPA, ACCA, CMA).

• Hands-on Dutch VAT, ICP and Dutch GAAP / IFRS experience.

• Experience with Hong Kong entities (audit cycle, profits tax, company secretary).

• Transfer-pricing documentation and royalty/licence flows.

• Odoo or Exact Online, ideally a migration between systems.

• Payment-platform reconciliation (Stripe, Adyen, Airwallex) at high transaction volume.

• Experience serving European clients remotely as an independent freelancer, ideally startups or scale-ups.



How you work

• You own the numbers and flag problems early, with a proposed fix.

• You build processes and controls that scale, and document them so they can be checked, repeated and automated.

• You know where your expertise ends and when to bring in the accountant.



Tools: Exact Online (moving to Odoo), Stripe, Airwallex, ABN AMRO, Revolut, Nmbrs, Google Workspace, Slack, 



Hours: Full-time (40 hrs/week)

Contract: Independent contractor (no agencies or BPO providers)

Location: Fully remote with CET business hours

Compensation: Hourly rate [TBD — in EUR or USD], invoiced monthly

Start date: [TBD]
